thread:
Ari (design): Heads-up: I prototyped a 'warning layer' that appears over a rollout row when a user opens the rollback action. Purpose: reduce accidental rollbacks and surface snapshot + op-id without a full modal. Figma: https://figma.redwood/warning-layer-v1
Luca (product): Love the lightweight approach. Two concerns: (1) will users miss that rollback is async? (2) do we need an extra confirmation for large traffic jumps (>30%)?
Chen (frontend): Implementation note: the layer is an inline overlay (not a page modal) so it won't break keyboard flow if we trap focus properly. We can render op-id from backend and show a tiny progress bar. Undo toast afterwards is easy.
Mira (eng-runtime): We'll return op-id + estimated duration in ms. UX must say "Rollback started (op-5553) — ETA ~75s". Also +1 on a confirmation checkbox when the rollback will affect more than 30% traffic. That prevents accidental global changes.
Oli (a11y): Accessibility rules: overlay must be a focused alertdialog with aria-modal=true so screen readers announce it. For non-destructive snapshot creation use aria-live=polite. Include clear SR copy: "Confirm rollback to v2.4. This will redirect 45% of traffic. Snapshot snap-2025-09-21-555 created." Provide keyboard shortcut to escape. Avoid tiny hit targets.
Ari (design): Copy candidates:
- Candidate 1 (safer): Primary = "Create snapshot and rollback" (danger), checkbox for "I understand this will change live traffic" shown if >30%
- Candidate 2 (separate): Primary = "Create snapshot"; secondary = "Rollback (danger)" after snapshot success
- Candidate 3 (fast): Primary = "Rollback now"; tiny inline explanation + undo toast
Luca (product): I'm voting Candidate 2. Snapshot-first reduces support tickets. But enterprise customers might want Candidate 3 as an escape hatch. Maybe we enable Candidate 3 via a feature flag.
Chen (frontend): Candidate 2 is simplest to build and surfaces progress. For the overlay, I'll make sure focus moves into it, first element is the primary CTA, cancel returns focus to row. Also include aria-describedby linking to the op log.
Mira (eng-runtime): Backend-wise Candidate 2: we can chain snapshot->rollback ops and emit separate op-ids; UI should display both: "Snapshot created (snap-777) — Rollback started (op-5553)". Also recommend a debounce on rapid rollbacks.
Oli (a11y): For SR copy use assertive announce on rollback start: "Rollback to v2.4 started; ETA ~75 seconds; operation op-5553" and polite updates for progress pings. For the confirmation checkbox make the label explicit: "I understand this will change live traffic and may cause user-visible behavior".
Ari (design): Visual notes: the warning layer will have a soft yellow border and caution icon (aria-hidden). For colorblind folks include a worded banner: "This action will change live traffic by +45%". For compact rows collapse the layer to a compact popover but keep full SR text in DOM.
Luca (product): quick reactions: :+1: Candidate 2, :heart: Candidate 1, :thinking_face: Candidate 3
Ari (design): :+1:
Chen (frontend): :+1:
Mira (eng-runtime): :heart:
Oli (a11y): :+1: (Candidate 2 with explicit SR labels)
DeployBot: Snapshot snap-20250921-777 created for canary v2.4
Ari (design): Action items: 1) I'll update Figma to Candidate 2 and add compact-popover variant 2) Chen will prototype overlay + focus trap + toast 3) Mira will include op-id + ETA in API and emit separate op-ids for snapshot+rollback 4) Oli will draft SR copy and confirm aria-modal behavior. Follow-up review Wednesday. Thanks all!
